prompt: Five machines run at 70% CPU each and the target is 50%. What size does the autoscaler recommend?
hint: Total work divided by the target, rounded up.

prompt: What does a CPU target of 60% buy compared with 90%?
hint: What is the other 40% for?

choices.text: A cheaper group, since fewer machines are needed at 60%
choices.why: A lower target needs more machines for the same work.

choices.text: A faster processor for each machine in the group
choices.why: The target does not change the machine type.

choices.text: Headroom for a burst while new machines start
choices.why: Right. 90% is cheaper and leaves no room.

choices.text: Fewer health check failures
choices.why: Health checks are a separate thing.

prompt: Why does the group in autoscale/main.tf have no target_size?
hint: Who sets the size once an autoscaler is attached?

choices.text: The autoscaler sets the size now
choices.why: Right. One of them has to own the size.

choices.text: Regional groups do not accept target_size
choices.why: Lesson 4's regional group had one.

choices.text: target_size is replaced by max_replicas
choices.why: max_replicas is a ceiling, not a size.

choices.text: The plan fails when both are present
choices.why: The plan would accept both; the conflict shows later.

prompt: The ___ is the setting that keeps a bug from scaling the group to a hundred machines; in Terraform it is max_replicas.
hint: The opposite of a floor.

prompt: cpu_utilization { target = 1.5 } plans cleanly. What does gcloud's help tell you about it?
hint: The range in the flag's description.

choices.text: That 1.5 means 150% and is fine for burstable machines
choices.why: The range is 0.0 to 1.0.

choices.text: That the target is in vCPUs, so 1.5 is one and a half
choices.why: It is a fraction of utilisation.

choices.text: Nothing: the help has no range for this flag
choices.why: It states 0.0 to 1.0.

choices.text: The target must be from 0.0 to 1.0, so Compute Engine refuses it
choices.why: Right. The plan does not check the range.

prompt: Which signal suits a photo worker that drains a Pub/Sub subscription?
hint: Measure the work waiting.

choices.text: CPU utilisation, as for the web group
choices.why: A queue can grow while CPU sits low.

choices.text: Undelivered messages per machine
choices.why: Right. It scales out before anybody waits.

choices.text: Load-balancing utilisation
choices.why: A worker pulling from a queue has no balancer in front.

choices.text: A daily schedule from nine to six
choices.why: Uploads do not keep office hours.

prompt: With single_instance_assignment = 50, how many workers does a backlog of 730 messages ask for?
hint: Divide and round up.

prompt: Why can the photos autoscaler have min_replicas = 0 when the web one keeps 3?
hint: What does an empty queue mean?

choices.text: Metric-based autoscalers ignore min_replicas
choices.why: They respect it; 0 was chosen.

choices.text: Workers are cheaper than web machines, so zero is allowed
choices.why: Price is not what allows zero.

choices.text: With an empty queue there is no work, and nobody waits for a worker
choices.why: Right. A web group must answer the first visitor at once.

choices.text: Pub/Sub keeps one worker running for free
choices.why: Pub/Sub runs no machines.

prompt: An autoscaler follows CPU and a custom metric. The metric gets stuck at a high stale value. What happens?
hint: Which recommendation wins?

choices.text: The group stays near its maximum until somebody notices
choices.why: Right. The largest recommendation wins.

choices.text: The CPU signal overrides it, since CPU is measured live
choices.why: No signal overrides another; the largest size wins.

choices.text: The autoscaler averages the two and settles in the middle
choices.why: It takes the largest, not the average.

choices.text: The autoscaler disables the metric after ten minutes
choices.why: Nothing disables it automatically.

prompt: When several signals give different sizes, the autoscaler uses the ___ of them.
hint: The safe direction.

prompt: What does a scaling schedule with min_required_replicas = 6 do during its window?
hint: A floor or a size?

choices.text: Holds the group at exactly six
choices.why: CPU can still add more on top.

choices.text: Adds six to whatever the CPU rule wants
choices.why: It is a floor, not an addition.

choices.text: Removes machines above six to save money
choices.why: A schedule never makes the group smaller.

choices.text: Keeps at least six
choices.why: Right. It raises the minimum for the window.

prompt: Why does the weekday schedule start at eight when traffic rises at nine?
hint: What happens between creation and serving?

choices.text: Cron cannot express nine o'clock in São Paulo
choices.why: It can; the hour is a choice.

choices.text: New machines need time to boot and pass health checks
choices.why: Right. They should be serving when the rise arrives.

choices.text: Schedules always fire an hour late
choices.why: They fire when written.

choices.text: Machines are cheaper before nine
choices.why: Prices do not change by the hour.

prompt: The snapshot schedule of lesson 3 was in UTC. What does time_zone = "America/Sao_Paulo" do here?
hint: How is the cron line read?

choices.text: It moves the machines to São Paulo for the window
choices.why: Placement is the group's, not the schedule's.

choices.text: It converts the schedule to UTC before saving it
choices.why: The zone is stored and used as written.

choices.text: The cron line is read in São Paulo time
choices.why: Right. Eight stays eight in the shop's own clock.

choices.text: It is decoration; the autoscaler always uses UTC
choices.why: It decides how the expression is read.

prompt: A schedule lifts the floor from 3 to 5 e2-standard-2 machines (0.06701142 USD an hour) for 8 hours on each of 20 weekdays. At most, what do the extra machines cost, in USD, to the cent?
hint: Two extra machines, 160 hours each.

prompt: The Black Friday schedule names 0 0 27 11 *. What must the team remember next year?
hint: Does the sale fall on the same date every year?

choices.text: It fires every 27 November; change it after the sale
choices.why: Right. A sale whose date moves needs a schedule written for each year.

choices.text: To renew the schedule, which expires after one firing
choices.why: A cron schedule repeats; that is the problem.

choices.text: Nothing: the line fires on Black Friday every year
choices.why: It fires on 27 November every year, whatever day the sale is.

choices.text: To switch it to UTC so it fires at midnight
choices.why: São Paulo time is what makes it midnight in the shop.

prompt: What does the initialisation period, cooldown_period in Terraform, tell the autoscaler?
hint: A new machine's numbers are misleading for a while.

choices.text: How long to wait between two scale-in steps
choices.why: That is the scale-in control's window.

choices.text: How long a machine may run before it is replaced
choices.why: Nothing replaces a machine for its age here.

choices.text: How long the group pauses after a failed health check
choices.why: Health checks have their own thresholds.

choices.text: How long to ignore a new machine's numbers
choices.why: Right. Its startup CPU is not real load.

prompt: A group at 12 machines has a scale-in control of at most 3 machines per 10 minutes. The load needs 3. How many minutes at least until the group is at 3?
hint: Nine machines to remove, three per window.

prompt: A new group created yesterday is given predictive_method = "OPTIMIZE_AVAILABILITY". What should the team expect this week?
hint: What does prediction learn from?

choices.text: Machines started a day ahead of every rise
choices.why: It has no history yet to predict from.

choices.text: No forecasts for about three days
choices.why: Right. Prediction learns from the group's own past.

choices.text: A refusal, since prediction needs a load balancer
choices.why: It works on the CPU signal.

choices.text: The CPU target ignored in favour of the forecast
choices.why: The target still applies; prediction adds machines ahead of it.

prompt: The initialisation period is set to 10 seconds for machines that take 3 minutes to start. What goes wrong?
hint: What does the autoscaler read after 10 seconds?

choices.text: The machines are deleted by autohealing
choices.why: That is the health check's initial delay, a different setting.

choices.text: Nothing: a shorter period only makes scaling faster
choices.why: It makes the autoscaler read startup work as load.

choices.text: Startup CPU looks like load and adds machines
choices.why: Right. Set it to the measured start time.

choices.text: The schedule fires ten seconds early
choices.why: Schedules do not read this setting.

prompt: Before scaling in, the autoscaler uses the highest recommendation of the last ten minutes; this is the ___ period.
hint: It waits for the load to settle.

prompt: Order these by how far ahead of the load each one acts, from furthest ahead to the one that only reacts.
hint: A person writing a date knows the most.
items: A schedule for a known sale
trap: A queue measures work waiting, so it acts before CPU rises; but it still waits for the work to arrive, unlike a forecast.

prompt: Match each setting to the problem it solves.
hint: Floor, ceiling, start-up, way down.

pairs.right: A quiet night leaving no machine in a zone
A bug scaling the group to a hundred machines
Startup CPU read as real load
Load that falls and comes straight back

prompt: The web group scales on CPU, but at lunchtime users wait and CPU stays at 30%: each request waits on the database. What should change first?
hint: More web machines would wait on the same database.

choices.text: Look at the database, since the group is not the bottleneck
choices.why: Right. No autoscaling setting of the web group fixes this.

choices.text: Lower the CPU target to 20% so more machines start
choices.why: More web machines add load to the bottleneck.

choices.text: Add predictive autoscaling for the lunchtime rise
choices.why: Predicting more web machines does not help a slow database.

choices.text: Switch to load-balancing utilisation
choices.why: It would scale the web group up, onto the same slow database.

prompt: Three machines at 40%, 50% and 60% CPU, target 0.5. What size does recommend.py print?
hint: 1.5 machines of work.

prompt: What can this lab show about the autoscaler, and what can it not?
hint: There is no group running.

choices.text: It can show the group growing under a load test
choices.why: There is no group to grow.

choices.text: It can show nothing, since the autoscaler is remote
choices.why: The policy and the arithmetic run here.

choices.text: Only the schedules, since they are cron
choices.why: Schedules are planned like everything else; none fires here.

choices.text: The policy and the arithmetic, not the scaling
choices.why: Right. The plan shows the policy; recommend.py shows the rule.
